title: What does FINRA Rule 3110(a)(7) require for the annual compliance meeting?
description: FINRA Rule 3110(a)(7) annual compliance meeting: who attends, remote delivery conditions in 3110.04, supervisor training and evidence, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: FINRA Rule 3110(a)(7) requires every registered representative and registered principal of a FINRA member firm to take part, at least once a year, in an interview or meeting at which compliance matters relevant to their activities are discussed. Supplementary Material 3110.04 allows remote or on-demand delivery only if the firm can show each person attended the entire meeting and could ask questions and receive timely answers.
keyTakeaways: Rule 3110(a)(7) applies to each registered representative and registered principal, individually or collectively, no less than annually, in a meeting or interview run by persons the member designates.

Supplementary Material 3110.04 removes any in-person requirement but sets two conditions for other formats: proof of attendance for the entire meeting, and a timely way to ask questions and get answers.
Rule 3110(a)(6) separately requires reasonable efforts to determine that all supervisory personnel are qualified, by experience or training, for their assigned responsibilities.
Under FINRA Rule 1240(b)(2)(D), participation in the annual compliance training under Rule 3110(a)(7) may count toward a registered person's Firm Element continuing education.
The rule sets no hours or syllabus. The content must be compliance matters relevant to the attendees' activities, so a single generic session for every role is hard to defend.
regulator: Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), overseen by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
appliesTo: Every registered representative and registered principal of a member firm (annual compliance meeting)
All supervisory personnel (qualification by experience or training under Rule 3110(a)(6))
Persons the member designates to conduct the annual meeting or interview

blocks.text: Rule 3110(a)(7) makes an annual compliance meeting a minimum element of every member firm's supervisory system. It sits inside [FINRA Rule 3110 (Supervision)](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/rulebooks/finra-rules/3110), which requires each member to establish and maintain a system to supervise the activities of each associated person that is reasonably designed to achieve compliance with securities laws and FINRA rules. The rule text reads:

blocks.title: FINRA Rule 3110(a)(7)
blocks.text: "The participation of each registered representative and registered principal, either individually or collectively, no less than annually, in an interview or meeting conducted by persons designated by the member at which compliance matters relevant to the activities of the representative(s) and principal(s) are discussed. Such interview or meeting may occur in conjunction with the discussion of other matters and may be conducted at a central or regional location or at the representative's(') or principal's(') place of business."

Four points follow from the wording. Attendance is personal: every registered representative and every registered principal must participate, including senior principals. The firm chooses who runs it. The frequency is a floor, not a target, so a firm can hold more than one session. And the subject matter is defined by relevance: the compliance matters discussed must relate to the activities of the people in the room, which is why many firms run separate sessions for retail, institutional, investment banking and supervisory audiences.
The position on this page is stated as at November 2026 and is based on the rule text published on finra.org.

sections.heading: Can the annual compliance meeting be delivered online or on demand?

blocks.text: Yes, provided the firm meets two conditions in Supplementary Material 3110.04. The supplementary material states that a member "is not required to conduct in-person meetings" and names on-demand webcasts or courses, video conferences, interactive classroom settings, telephone, and other electronic means as acceptable methods.

The first condition is full attendance. FINRA's own example for an on-demand webcast describes each registered person using a unique user ID and password, a platform that tracks time spent, click-as-you-go confirmation, and an attestation of completion at the end. The second condition is two-way access: each person must be able to ask questions about the presentation and receive answers in a timely fashion, for example by email to a presenter or a central address, or by telephone hotline, with responses given directly or posted on the firm's intranet.

blocks.title: Practical test
blocks.text: If a registered person could skip to the end of an on-demand module, or had no route to ask a question and get an answer, the session probably does not satisfy 3110.04. A completion flag in the learning system is not enough on its own; the record should show time on task, in-session confirmations, and the question channel offered.

sections.heading: What training does Rule 3110 expect of supervisors?

blocks.text: Rule 3110(a)(6) requires the member to use reasonable efforts to determine that all supervisory personnel are qualified, "either by virtue of experience or training," to carry out their assigned responsibilities. Unlike the annual meeting, this is not a fixed-frequency event. It is a standing duty that applies when a person is designated a supervisor and whenever responsibilities change.

Other parts of Rule 3110 shape what supervisor training has to cover. Rule 3110(b)(6) requires the written supervisory procedures to set out the titles, registration status, locations and responsibilities of each supervisory person, and to keep a record of designated supervisory personnel and the dates of designation for at least three years, the first two in an easily accessible place. Rule 3110(b)(4) requires reviews of correspondence and internal communications to be conducted by a registered principal and evidenced in writing. A supervisor who has not been trained on the firm's review procedures, escalation routes and evidence standards is unlikely to meet these duties.

sections.heading: How do written supervisory procedures connect to training?

blocks.text: Rule 3110(b)(7) requires each member to promptly amend its written supervisory procedures when securities laws, FINRA rules or its supervisory system change, and to promptly communicate the procedures and amendments to all associated persons to whom they are relevant. The annual meeting is a common place to reinforce those changes, but it cannot replace prompt communication: a rule change in March cannot wait for a December meeting.

Supplementary Material 3110.11 permits electronic communication of the procedures if they are readily accessible to the relevant associated persons, amendments are promptly posted, people are notified that relevant amendments have been made, the posted material is protected against unauthorized alteration, and current and prior versions are retained in line with SEA Rule 17a-4(e)(7). Those five conditions are, in effect, a version control and notification standard for policy content. See [how to maintain version control for training content](/guides/how-to-maintain-version-control-for-training-content).

sections.heading: Does the annual compliance meeting count toward FINRA continuing education?

blocks.text: It can. FINRA Rule 1240(b)(2)(D) states that a member may consider a registered person's participation in the member's annual compliance training under Rule 3110(a)(7), and in its anti-money laundering training under Rule 3310(e), toward the Firm Element requirement. The Firm Element itself, including the annual needs analysis and written training plan, is explained on the [FINRA continuing education requirements](/regulations/finra-continuing-education-requirements) page.

Counting is permissive, not automatic. If a firm credits the annual meeting toward the Firm Element, the Firm Element training plan should say so and the meeting content should map to the training needs the firm identified. The AML training that can also be credited is covered on the [FINRA Rule 3310 AML training](/regulations/finra-rule-3310-aml-program-training) page.

sections.heading: Which other annual Rule 3110 duties affect the training calendar?

blocks.text: Rule 3110(c)(1) requires a review, at least annually on a calendar-year basis, of the businesses in which the member engages, and sets inspection cycles: every office of supervisory jurisdiction (OSJ) and any branch office that supervises non-branch locations at least annually, and every non-supervising branch office at least every three years. Findings from these inspections are a natural input to the next annual compliance meeting agenda.

Rule changes also feed the agenda. For example, the SEC approved new FINRA Rule 3290 (Outside Activities Requirements) by an order published in the Federal Register on September 18, 2026. Firms should confirm the effective date on finra.org before scheduling training on it, but outside activities is the kind of topic that belongs in an annual meeting for every registered person.

sections.heading: What evidence should a firm keep for each Rule 3110 training duty?

blocks.text: A firm should be able to show, for each duty, who it applied to, when it was met, and what was covered. The table below maps the training-related elements of Rule 3110 to the audience, the frequency the rule sets, and the evidence an examiner would reasonably expect. It is an original planning aid, not FINRA text.

blocks.text: Reconciling the attendee list to the registered population is the step most often missed. Pull the list of registered persons from the firm's registration records at the start of the cycle, track each person to completion, and record the reason and makeup date for anyone who missed the main session. The [guide to preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) covers the record set in more detail.

sections.heading: How should a firm decide what the annual meeting covers?

blocks.text: Start from the activities of each audience, because relevance to those activities is the only content test the rule sets. A practical method is to list each business line's activities, map the FINRA and SEC obligations that apply to each, and then select topics where there were rule changes, inspection or exam findings, complaints, or near misses in the past year. The [guide to mapping training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations) sets out the mapping step.

items: Segment the registered population by activity (for example retail sales, institutional sales and trading, investment banking, principals and branch managers).
For each segment, list the obligations that apply and the year's changes, findings and complaint themes.
Draft an agenda per segment, with a shared core for firmwide topics.
Decide the delivery format and, for remote delivery, configure attendance tracking and the question channel to meet 3110.04.
Run the sessions, reconcile attendance to the registered population, and schedule makeups.
Record which content is credited toward the Firm Element under Rule 1240(b)(2)(D), if any.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each Rule 3110 element to the roles it applies to and the evidence it requires before any meeting content is written, so the agenda for each audience is traceable to the activities and obligations that justify it. When a rule or procedure changes, the affected topics and audiences are identified from that map rather than by rereading every deck. More detail is on the [financial services](/industries/financial-services) page.

faqs.q: Do registered principals have to attend the annual compliance meeting?
faqs.a: Yes. Rule 3110(a)(7) applies to each registered representative and each registered principal. There is no carve-out for senior principals or for persons who also conduct the meeting. Principals can attend a session designed for supervisors, provided the compliance matters discussed are relevant to their activities.

faqs.q: Can the annual compliance meeting be combined with other business meetings?
faqs.a: Yes. The rule text states that the interview or meeting may occur in conjunction with the discussion of other matters. The compliance portion still needs to be identifiable, with its own agenda items and attendance evidence, so the firm can show compliance matters relevant to each attendee were actually discussed.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum length for the annual compliance meeting?
faqs.a: No. Rule 3110(a)(7) and Supplementary Material 3110.04 set no minimum duration or hours. For remote delivery, the firm must ensure each person attends the entire meeting, which is why FINRA's example refers to tracking time spent on an on-demand webcast.

faqs.q: Does an individual interview satisfy the rule instead of a group meeting?
faqs.a: Yes. The rule allows participation "either individually or collectively" in "an interview or meeting." An individual interview with a designated person can work for small firms or for people who miss the group session, as long as relevant compliance matters are discussed and the interview is documented.

faqs.q: Who should conduct the annual compliance meeting?
faqs.a: The rule says the meeting is conducted by persons designated by the member. It does not require a principal or a compliance officer. Firms typically designate compliance staff, supervisory principals or both, and record the designation alongside the meeting materials.

factCheck.claim: Rule 3110(a)(7) requires each registered representative and registered principal, individually or collectively, no less than annually, to participate in an interview or meeting conducted by persons designated by the member at which relevant compliance matters are discussed.

Supplementary Material 3110.04 states in-person meetings are not required; other methods must ensure each registered person attends the entire meeting (example: unique user ID and password, time tracking, click-as-you-go confirmation, attestation) and can ask questions and receive timely answers.
Rule 3110(a)(6) requires reasonable efforts to determine that all supervisory personnel are qualified, either by virtue of experience or training, to carry out their assigned responsibilities.
Rule 3110(b)(6)(B) requires a record of designated supervisory personnel and dates of designation preserved for not less than three years, the first two in an easily accessible place.
Supplementary Material 3110.11 sets five conditions for electronic communication of written supervisory procedures, including retention of current and prior versions under SEA Rule 17a-4(e)(7).

Rule 3110(c)(1) requires an annual calendar-year review of the businesses, annual inspection of every OSJ and supervising branch office, and inspection of non-supervising branch offices at least every three years.
FINRA Rule 1240(b)(2)(D) allows a member to consider participation in annual compliance training under Rule 3110(a)(7) and AML training under Rule 3310(e) toward the Firm Element requirement.
The SEC order approving FINRA Rule 3290 (Outside Activities Requirements) was published in the Federal Register on September 18, 2026.
